episodes.186076: A rare fall severe thunderstorm hail event occurred during the morning of November 6th.  There were several reports of large hail ranging from an inch to as much as an inch and a half in diameter.
episodes.186277: The start of a more active weather pattern culminated in the passage of a Pacific storm into the region. The incoming cold front brought strong, gusty west-southwest winds, increased chances for more widespread moderate rain showers,  and mountain snow. Snow-levels dropping to or near higher Sierra pass level brought increased travel difficulties. An incoming cold front and strong Pacific jet stream sustained the gusty conditions across the Sierra ridges into western Nevada.
episodes.187131: The combination of a surface trough over the eastern Caribbean and an|upper-level trough north and west of the region promoted wet and unstable conditions during the week of November 6-9. This produced showers and thunderstorms over the eastern and northern sections of Puerto Rico, including the San Juan Metro area. Urban and flash flooding was observed across these areas.

events.narrative: A Cocorahs station (CA-LS-2) located 3.5 mi SSW Susanville, CA, and a trained spotter located 5.0 mi WNW of Susanville, CA, reported storm total rainfall amounts of 0.99 and  0.81 inches respectively.
A CO-OP observer (FARC1) located 2.3 mi NW of Floriston, CA, reported a total rainfall amount of 0.91 inches.
An ASOS station (KTVL-South Lake Tahoe Airport) located 3.0 mi N of Meyers, CA, reported a total rainfall amount of 0.68 inches.
